# Twitch + GrowthBook
Date: 2026-09-23 | Duration: 62.18000030517578m

## Summary
Twitch is evaluating alternatives to EPO after Datadog’s acquisition led to support concerns and created a required migration before the contract ends in Q1 2027. GrowthBook described prior migrations for Anthropic, Discord, and Twitter, including Anthropic’s migration in under a month with custom importers for thousands of metrics. The discussion covered Twitch’s 50 to 80 concurrent monthly experiments, incremental data refreshes, pre-aggregation, configurable Redshift data lifecycles, and recent-data windows for long-term holdouts. GrowthBook supports cloud, self-hosted, hybrid, CDN-fronted, client-side, and server-side feature-flag delivery, aligning with Twitch’s custom CDN and 10-minute TTL. Migration risks include reproducing EPO’s long-term holdout hashing and potentially running both SDKs in parallel. GrowthBook also presented certified metrics, ownership metadata, scoped search, metric slices, templates, and possible lifecycle-management improvements. Engineering follow-ups and a platform demo are planned.

## Keywords
feature flags, experimentation platform, migration, holdout experiments, scalability, metric management

## Action Items

**Mengru Fu**
Coordinate with Jessica and GrowthBook team to set up a follow-up call involving Twitch engineering leaders to discuss SDKs and feature flag implementation in detail (01:00:17)

**Jessica**
Serve as main point of contact to involve Twitch engineering team for the next detailed technical follow-up meeting with GrowthBook (01:00:28)

**Christian Liebenow**
Share a 5-minute demo video of GrowthBook’s platform with the Twitch team for asynchronous review before the next meeting (01:00:31)
Collaborate with Jessica to schedule the next detailed technical follow-up meeting involving Twitch engineering leads and GrowthBook team (01:00:31)

**GrowthBook Team**
Prepare for a detailed demo covering SDKs and feature flagging implementation tailored for Twitch’s engineering team for the next meeting (01:00:00)

# Twitch + GrowthBook
Date: 2026-10-02 | Duration: 63.61000061035156m

## Summary
GrowthBook described a flexible integration model for Twitch, including multi-language SDKs with consistent bucketing, local or remote evaluation, configurable payload distribution, Redshift event tracking, GitHub metric syncing, multiple identifiers, and OpenFeature compatibility. It outlined experimentation capabilities such as Bayesian analysis, transparent SQL metrics, segmentation, cross-identifier joins, namespaces, automated rollouts, guardrails, and rollback triggers. GrowthBook also discussed mobile SDK customization, version-based targeting, remote filtering, and mobile-specific rollout controls. Its developer tools support real-time flag inspection, attribute overrides, exposure simulation, evaluation traces, and stale-flag cleanup. For migration, GrowthBook cited a large customer transition completed in two weeks using custom importers, shadow environments, sticky bucketing, and Redshift validation, supported by shared Slack channels, training, office hours, and 24/7 support. Twitch and GrowthBook planned broader demonstrations, technical discussions, and potential co-design of experiment planning and collision-management features.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, SDK integration, Experiment migration, Mobile rollout, Experiment collision, Open Feature
